interfaces.emptyDiscovered: No interfaces discovered yet. They appear after an SNMP table walk runs — the node needs a bound SNMP credential and a table metric in its collection set.
interfaces.colNeighborsTitle: What this port is connected to, as the device reports it over CDP or LLDP. Click a name to see every neighbor on the port. A CDP neighbor is placed by the port's index; an LLDP neighbor only when the device names the port the same way as this list does, so a port can show — here while the Neighbors tab lists a neighbor for it.
interfaces.colAddressesTitle: The IP addresses configured on this port — every one of them, secondaries included — as the device lists them in its IP address tables, read once an hour. The first is shown; +N opens the full list, and hovering the cell shows them all. An address is written as ip/prefix length; one shown without a prefix is an address whose mask the device did not report in a readable form. — means the device lists no address on this port, or the address walk has not run yet.
interfaces.addressesHint: Matches any address on the port, in the ip/prefix spelling the column shows — so a secondary hidden behind +N still matches. 10.221. finds the ports carrying that range, /30 the point-to-point links.
interfaces.colOperTitle: Operational status — whether the interface is up or down
interfaces.colInOutTitle: Traffic now. The background shades by utilization — how much of the link's own rate is in use — from green to red. A port that does not report its rate is left unshaded.
interfaces.duplexHint: How the link negotiated: full duplex sends both ways at once, half duplex one way at a time. Mostly a copper diagnostic — one end forced to full against an auto-negotiating peer is a classic cause of a link that works but is slow. Fibre ports usually show nothing, and that is correct: no half duplex exists above 1 Gbps, so there is nothing to negotiate.

duplexEmpty.unknown: This device did not report a duplex mode for this port. Normal on fibre — 802.3 defines no half duplex above 1 Gbps — and on ports that are down.
duplexEmpty.notApplicable: Not an Ethernet port, so duplex does not apply.

interfaces.mediaHint: The physical medium the port runs — 1000BASE-T for copper, 1000BASE-SX or -LX for fibre. Read from the device's MAU table, falling back to the transceiver's own part number. Many devices do not report it at all, and then this column stays empty: it is a gap in what the device will say, not a fault. Matching also searches the transceiver part number, so a search for SX still finds a module whose medium could not be resolved.

mediaEmpty.unknown: This device did not report a medium for this port, and no transceiver part number was readable. Common — the MAU table is widely unimplemented.
mediaEmpty.notApplicable: Not an Ethernet port, so it has no physical medium.
